parts.name: Anulus fibrosus
parts.attachment_or_location: outer concentric lamellae, obliquely-crossing collagen fiber orientation alternating between layers
parts.function_note: the alternating (roughly +/-30 degree) fiber angle between adjacent lamellae lets the anulus resist torsional as well as tensile loading; its outer fibers are innervated and can be a direct pain source (discogenic pain) even without frank herniation.
parts.source: Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- intervertebral disc anulus fibrosus/nucleus pulposus structure and biomechanics.

parts.name: Nucleus pulposus
parts.attachment_or_location: central gelatinous core, proteoglycan- and water-rich
parts.function_note: functions hydrostatically, distributing compressive load radially outward onto the anulus; its water content (and thus disc height/hydrostatic function) declines progressively with age, a normal degenerative process distinct from frank pathology.
parts.source: Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- intervertebral disc anulus fibrosus/nucleus pulposus structure and biomechanics.

function: The cervical spine's intervertebral discs, modeled here as one grouped entity per region (matching the grouped-vertebrae convention already used for cervical_vertebrae in data/skeleton/bones.json) rather than one entry per motion segment. Each disc is a fibrocartilaginous joint (symphysis) permitting limited multi-axial motion between adjacent vertebral bodies while transmitting and distributing axial load.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- intervertebral disc anulus fibrosus/nucleus pulposus structure and biomechanics.
